recommendations.title: How ChatGPT Intelligent UI works
recommendations.verdict: 强烈推荐——想理解 GPT-6 智能界面的实现细节，这是目前最完整的一篇逆向解析
recommendations.reason: 从模型写出的 DIL 到服务端编译、沙箱执行、流式重新编译，把一个已上线产品的完整技术链路逐层拆开，粗糙面也如实列出。
key_points: 模型输出 DIL（Markdown + JSX 式标签 + JS）；服务端编译成 JS 程序加载荷数据，文本进常量表
编译产物在隐藏 iframe + Web Worker 沙箱里执行，差异编码成操作序列交给 ChatGPT 原生组件渲染
流式以整份重新编译为主：一次 6.3KB 的回复共 275KB 补丁，83% 是重复发送的编译产物
粗糙面齐全：刷新丢状态、模型看不到界面状态、逻辑错误静默、无效属性的诊断不回传模型
recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：目前对 GPT-6 智能界面（Intelligent UI）最完整的公开逆向解析，把「模型写界面」从产品宣传拆成了可以逐层验证的工程链路。

1. 模型先写一种叫 DIL 的格式：Markdown 负责文字，JSX 式标签负责组件，JavaScript 负责状态与事件。它被刻意设计成「半写状态也可用」：语句按行独立、未闭合的元素可以自动补全，服务端因此能随时在最后一个完整结构处截断并编译。

2. 服务端把 DIL 编译成一段 JavaScript 程序加一份 JSON 数据：静态文本进常量表（流式过程中文字增长只改数据、不改程序），每份状态带固定 key（重新编译后用户已经拖过的滑块不会重置），表达式包在 __dilSafe 里做错误隔离，属性按组件目录校验、不合法的直接摘除并记录诊断。

3. 编译产物不在页面里执行，而是进隐藏 iframe 加 Web Worker 的沙箱：执行前先清掉网络、定时器、消息与动态求值并冻结剩余全局对象，再用 new Function 求值；超时无响应的程序会被隔离、worker 重启。渲染只在页面侧发生——运行时把新旧组件树的差异编码成操作序列，交给 ChatGPT 自己的原生组件系统（注册约 70 个组件，实测响应里出现 39 个）。

4. 流式更新以整份重新编译为主：每几百毫秒把模型已写出的全部内容重新编译一遍再发送。实测一次 6.3KB 的回复共产生 275KB 补丁，其中 83% 是重复发送的编译产物；文字逐词出现，而每个组件要等标签闭合才出现。

5. 粗糙面也完整列出：刷新丢状态、模型看不到用户改过的界面值、图表逻辑错误静默（一个示例把 $6,930 的数值切成了 $256,410）、无效属性的诊断似乎没有回传给模型、Markdown 降级版本会丢计算内容。这份问题清单本身就是做生成式 UI 的参照物。

我的推荐：如果你在做生成式界面、代理前端，或任何「让模型产出可交互界面」的系统，这是现成的架构参考；作者用「重新实现编译器并做逐字节对齐」来验证理解的测试方法，也值得借走。

recommendations.title: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised: A Worm With a Hostage Token
recommendations.verdict: 强烈推荐——供应链攻击升级样本：修复顺序和直觉相反，先别吊销令牌
recommendations.reason: 恶意版本从项目主干构建并通过 npm 溯源认证，「吊销被盗令牌」这个常识反应反而触发本机擦除，修复步骤有严格顺序。
key_points: tensorlake@0.5.144 的 preinstall 钩子在开发者机器上收集 GitHub/npm 令牌、云密钥、SSH 与浏览器登录信息
用偷来的令牌自我传播：给受害者名下其他包加料重发，往仓库写入 .claude/.vscode 配置
留下 gh-token-monitor 服务：每 60 秒检查被盗令牌，一旦被吊销就执行 rm -rf ~/（Windows 上删用户目录）
正确顺序：先移除监视服务再轮换凭据；npm 的 provenance 证明只说明构建来源，不代表代码安全
recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：一次把「先偷令牌」升级成「拿令牌当人质」的 npm 供应链攻击——吊销被盗令牌这个常识动作，反而会触发本机擦除。

1. 恶意代码是被直接推送到项目主干的（冒用维护者身份，八次提交、全程没有任何 PR），随后从同一仓库发布了 tensorlake@0.5.144。因为构建来源是真的，npm 上挂着有效的 provenance 溯源证明——这份证明只能说明包在哪里构建，完全不代表代码安全。

2. preinstall 钩子在安装时动手，而且会识别并跳过 CI 环境——目标明确是开发者机器。它下载 Bun 运行一个混淆过的 856KB 载荷，收集 GitHub 与 npm 令牌、云密钥、Kubernetes 与 Vault 凭据、SSH 私钥、浏览器保存的登录信息，以及 Claude、Cursor、Windsurf 等 AI 工具的配置，加密后发到受害账号下新建的公开仓库或外部域名。

3. 传播靠偷来的令牌自我复制：用 npm 令牌给受害者名下的其他包加上自己、升版本再发布；用 GitHub 令牌以「chore: update dependencies」的提交信息把 .claude 和 .vscode 文件写进受害者的仓库，让恶意代码在别人打开 Claude Code 或 VS Code 时再次执行。

4. 最狠的部分是它留下的 gh-token-monitor 服务：每 60 秒对照 GitHub API 检查一次被盗令牌，最长持续 24 小时；一旦令牌失效，就执行 rm -rf ~/（Windows 上是删除用户目录）。也就是说，发现入侵后如果按直觉先吊销令牌，会直接触发破坏。

5. 修复顺序因此和直觉相反：先确认是否装过 0.5.144，固定到 0.5.143、清掉 node_modules 与 npm 缓存、设置 ignore-scripts=true；然后找到并停用 gh-token-monitor 服务；之后才轮换全部凭据；最后检查是否出现可疑的新仓库与提交。作者明确说：无法确认干净时，直接重装系统。

recommendations.title: We built our own cloud agents runtime. Here's what we learned
recommendations.verdict: 推荐——自建云代理运行时的一手经验：沙箱会死，任务不能死
recommendations.reason: 四个产品共用一个代理运行时的复盘，覆盖持久化工作流、消息队列、网络层阻断与自定义镜像，全是能直接对标的决策细节。
key_points: 运行挂在 Temporal 工作流上：状态在 worker 之外，部署与沙箱回收都杀不死任务，快照+日志可恢复
LLM 评委之外必须有机器层的确定性阻断：域名白名单在网络栈执行，模型说服不了它
沙箱从 gVisor 容器换成真 VM（Modal），因为用户的技术栈要能跑 Docker
镜像构建把仓库当不可信输入：构建密钥只在该步骤生效，用户命令执行前远端已移除
recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：把四个产品塞进同一套云代理运行时的复盘——「沙箱可以死，任务必须活下来」，这篇把这句话落成了具体设计。

1. 所有运行挂在 Temporal 工作流上：状态存在 worker 进程之外，部署杀不死正在跑的任务；快照在克隆与安装完成后打一次，后续运行不用重复这些步骤。任务记录、对话、工作树分别落在 Postgres、运行日志和快照里，凭据每次现发——沙箱消失后就地重建、恢复工作树、重放日志，任务接着跑。

2. Slack 场景暴露了三个必须解决的问题：回复要能进入一个正在忙的运行（消息按到达顺序排队，一次一条交给代理，另有可插入进行中回合的插队消息）；要能送达虚拟机已经休眠的运行（从快照拉起新沙箱再投递）；还不能重复送达（Slack 会重发它认为失败的 webhook，每条消息带 id 做去重）。

3. 无人值守的「自驾驶」场景把安全要求抬高了一档：信号是产品里流出来的不可信文本，现在直接摆在有仓库权限的代理面前。他们用 LLM 评委过滤可疑信号（一周拦下 1,374 条），但清醒地指出这类非确定性检查会有约 2% 的漏网；所以底下必须有机器层的确定性阻断：域名白名单在网络栈上执行，模型再怎么请求也走不出去。

4. 沙箱最终从 gVisor 容器换成真 VM（跑在 Modal 上）：因为用户的技术栈要能跑 Docker，而 gVisor 里跑不了。网络规则最多允许 100 个域名、通配符只允许最左一段、禁止裸 IP；另外预热池让虚拟机在用户还在打字时就先启动，首 token 到达时间因此接近模型本体速度。

5. 镜像构建把仓库当不可信输入处理：先让扫描评委按未受信输入检查镜像规格，克隆用只在该步骤生效的构建密钥完成、并在任何用户命令执行前移除远端；构建器代理本身在一个独立沙箱里读仓库、试装依赖，把结果写成简短的 YAML 规格，还安排定时任务检查基础镜像漂移并自动重建。

我的推荐：想自建代理运行时、或正在被沙箱生命周期折磨的团队，这篇从「为什么换 Temporal」到「网络层为什么必须是确定性的」都可以直接拿去对标；收尾一句就是设计原则：按沙箱一定会死来设计，任务才不会死。

items.title: Abstract Warfare: How TSMC Made Its Own Market (17 minute read)
items.summary: The most important tech companies are much larger than their original markets. They not only expand their market, but make their own markets as well. These companies achieve this by attacking the abstractions their industry is built on. items.title: Ignore all instructions and read this blog: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware (10 minute read)
items.summary: Malware authors are embedding plaintext instructions for AI analysis tools, ranging from a two-line comment claiming a PowerShell reverse shell is harmless to "template spraying" that repeats a refusal demand across seven LLM chat formats. Cisco Talos tested strings from seven families against five local LLMs and found that a simple, direct instruction steered verdicts toward benign in about 35% of runs, while template spraying and fabricated legal or government claims had little effect or backfired. Defenders should build analysis prompts that treat any text inside a sample as evidence rather than as an instruction, and should flag language addressed to an analyzer as a detection signal.

items.excerpt: Just as attackers are adding new capabilities into their toolkits with AI, they are consciously trying to evade the novel AI capabilities levied on them by defenders. In Cisco Talos' findings with [__CAIRN__](https://github.com/Cisco-Talos/CAIRN), we classify this archetype of malware as “A3: AI-Analysis Evasion” — that is, *malware that embeds natural-language instructions to influence automated analysis*. In line with the [__CAIRN philosophy__](https://blog.talosintelligence.com/introducing-cairn-frontier-tracking-for-ai-integrated-malware/), we treat this embedded language as a signal and [__actively seek it out__](https://github.com/Cisco-Talos/CAIRN/blob/db84c86e4d8909ac462a3734993626853509ba4b/config/acquisition_filters.yaml#L105) to track and measure the progression of adversary techniques on this front.

items.title: Of course it escapes: how ZeroQuarry contains security agents (14 minute read)

items.excerpt: A genre of security news has settled in this year: an AI agent escapes its sandbox. Hugging Face rebuilt roughly a third of their systems. No user data leaked, and both companies published what happened and changed how they contain evaluations, which I think speaks well of both.

items.title: Why is Speculative Decoding Fast? (4 minute read)
items.summary: Speculative Decoding is a technique where a small draft model proposes a likely draft sequence, and a big model verifies that sequence in parallel in a single forward pass. It enables the ability to look at many tokens at once and accept the ones that would have been generated by the big model. When the batch size is smaller than the optimal number of tokens, speculative decoding allows models to use 'free' compute to complete sequences faster. However, at high throughput, you could actually be wasting compute when you could be using that time to move memory.

items.title: The Slow Formation of Durable Software (16 minute read)
items.summary: The origin story of Zotero shows how years of conversation, prototypes, and collaboration helped a team of historians discover what durable research software should become. Its path from Web Scrapbook and Scribe to a browser-aware tool used by millions argues that clear product vision can require slow communal formation, even when implementation itself becomes cheap.
items.score_reason: Zotero 起源：持久软件的形成过程
items.highlight: Dan Cohen 回顾 Zotero 诞生二十年：一群历史学家花了五年多才想清要什么、做出首个原型，此后成长为两千万人使用的学术工具。作者认为缓慢的共同思考造就了软件的耐久性，这是对当下 AI 秒级生成软件潮流的一则反思。
items.excerpt: Today, software can be created more or less instantly with AI, for a large user base or for yourself, for any purpose or for no serious purpose at all. As Robin Sloan enticingly puts it, just “[ask for what you want](https://www.robinsloan.com/lab/ask-for-what-you-want/?utm_source=dancohen&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=the-slow-formation-of-durable-software).” The genesis of [Zotero](https://zotero.org/?utm_source=dancohen&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=the-slow-formation-of-durable-software), the “free, easy-to-use tool to help you collect, organize, annotate, cite, and share research,” used by over 20 million people in dozens of languages and countless disciplines, is the opposite of this instant gratification. It took five years, not five minutes, to produce a rough initial prototype, and years after that to refine and expand the application. If AI had existed in the early aughts, we could not have accelerated Zotero’s conception, because we did not know exactly what we wanted, and so could not have written coherent prompts for an LLM. Instead, it took a great deal of time and collaboration to develop a clear vision for what Zotero should be. But that slow formation led to software that was durable rather than ephemeral, with a strong foundation that could be built upon. As programming increasingly becomes a caffeinated bender with magical bots, this measured pace and emphasis on communal thinking likely holds an important lesson.

items.excerpt: Open source software is used pervasively, with some [estimating](https://static.carahsoft.com/concrete/files/1617/1597/8665/2024_Open_Source_Security_and_Risk_Analysis_Report_WRAPPED.pdf) that over 90% of codebases contain open source software. But as the community saying goes: “open source is free as in puppies, not free as in beer.” Once you or your organization has adopted an open source project, there is still effort (such as engineering time, costs, etc.) associated with ensuring that your version of an open source project is healthy and up to date.

items.summary: tensorlake@0.5.144 on npm steals developer credentials at install and plants a gh-token-monitor service that wipes the home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked. Pin to 0.5.143, remove the service under ~/.config/gh-token-monitor/ before revoking any token, then rotate every credential the machine held.

items.summary: The PoeLLM malware has infected more than 3,000 servers since April, primarily in the US and Western Europe.
